newsitem.title: ITALY: Iraq says exported 750,000 bpd oil last week.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says exported 750,000 bpd oil last week.

text.p: Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said on Thursday that Iraq exported 750,000 barrels of oil per day (bpd) last week under a United Nations oil-for-food deal.
He told a news conference in Rome that the export figure compared with some 500,000 bpd last December when the deal began and when oil prices were much higher.
U.N. resolution 986, in operation since December 9, permits Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicine.
A $7 fall in oil prices from $25 to $18 for benchmark Brent since early January has seen Iraqi exports rise to meet the $2 billion dollar target.
Rasheed said Iraq's potential output capacity now was 2.5 million bpd, compared with 3.5 million bpd before Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait, which triggered U.N. sanctions.
"In a couple of months we could be up to three (million bpd) again," Rasheed said, adding it would be another year before Iraq could raise production capacity to 3.5 million barrels.
"When sanctions are lifted, we will revert to our pre-sanctions quota," he said, referring to Iraq's 1990 OPEC allocation of 3.14 million bpd.
But he said Iraq wanted to increase output capacity to six million bpd by exploiting massive unexplored reserves estimated by Baghdad at 214 billion barrels.
Iraq's proven and probable reserves, over and above possible reserves, already stand at 112 billion barrels or second only in the world to Saudi Arabia.
"We have to increase our production to at least six million, at least," he said.
Foreign oil companies are expected to a play a major role in expanding Iraqi output once sanctions are lifted.
Russia's LUKoil has signed to develop the seven billion barrel West Qurna field.
Rasheed said on Thursday that Italian Agip SpA was close to a deal to develop the 300,000 bpd Nasiriya oilfield.
He said he also expected to conclude an agreement with China for Iraq's Ahdab oilfield development.
Iraq also expected shortly to sign deals with French companies, he added. Total SA and Elf Aquitaine have said they are in negotiation with Iraq.
"Priority will be given to those (countries) who took a positive attitude towards alleviating Iraqi suffering over the centuries and more recently," said Rasheed.
The minister appealed to Italy and others not to listen to pressure from the United States, which he said wanted President Saddam Hussein removed before sanctions could be lifted.

"The agony of the Iraqi people has escalated to such an extent it has truly become a genocide in every definition of this word," he said. "There is absolutely no reason for this suffering to continue."

Rasheed said U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan was due to report to the Security Council at the start of May on the oil-for-food exchange and a U.N. team was currently in Baghdad monitoring the situation.
"I hope in his report (Annan) will say that what could be provided under Resolution 986 is much, much below the humanitarian needs of the Iraqi people," Rasheed said.
Annan said in Geneva earlier this month he expected the Security Council to renew the deal as it stands when it expires in June.
-- Jude Webber, Rome newsroom +396 678 2501
